edges.description: Germline null allele of the orthologous gene, producing whole-animal absence of TNAP rather than the reduced enzyme of most human genotypes.
edges.limitations: A complete null models the severe perinatal/infantile end of the human allelic spectrum; it cannot address the residual-activity genotypes that account for the milder childhood, adult, and odonto- forms.

edges.description: Defective bone mineralization with osteoblast changes appears postnatally, which the authors read as TNAP being dispensable for the initial mineral deposition but required to maintain it.
TNAP-null mice develop epileptic seizures and apnea before weaning, matching the seizure phenotype of severe infantile hypophosphatasia.
edges.limitations: This report does not establish the pyridoxal 5'-phosphate mechanism for the seizures - the authors instead hypothesize a compromised autonomic nervous system arising from absent TNAP in the developing neural tube. The seizure phenotype is therefore recapitulated; its attribution to B6 handling is not tested here. The mechanism is established instead in the independently derived Alpl<tm1Sor> line (PMID:7550313), curated as a separate model in this entry; it is not asserted for this allele on that basis.

edges.description: A human dominant missense allele reproduced at the orthologous locus, giving partial rather than complete loss of enzyme function.
edges.target: ALPL loss of function and TNAP deficiency

edges.description: The dentoalveolar arm of the node is reproduced - alveolar bone radiolucencies, resorptive lesions and osteoid accumulation - while the skeletal arm is not.
edges.limitations: The postcranial skeleton is normal by radiography, with no difference in femur length, cortical or trabecular structure, mineral density, or mechanical properties, so this model speaks only to the dentoalveolar half of the node. Acellular cementum changes were nonsignificant and did not measurably affect periodontal attachment.

edges.description: Establishes the full mechanistic chain this node names: TNAP loss impairs PLP metabolism, brain GABA falls, and seizures follow - with pyridoxal rescue closing the loop.
edges.limitations: Mouse PLP handling and the dietary rescue are not straightforwardly transferable to human dosing, and the rescued animals go on to develop defective dentition, so pyridoxine responsiveness in this model should not be read as a claim about long-term outcome in patients.

edges.description: Dental involvement appears once the animals survive the seizures, but the skeleton is reported as developing normally in this line.
edges.limitations: Normal skeletal development in a TNAP-null mouse is the opposite of the defining human phenotype and of what the tm1Jlm line shows, so this model is not usable for the skeletal arm of the node. The dentition defect is observed only in pyridoxal-rescued animals, which is a treated rather than a natural-history observation.

nodes.description: Loss-of-function variants in ALPL reduce tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNAP) activity. nodes.description: Homologous-recombination knockout of the mouse tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNAP) gene, generated alongside an embryonic alkaline phosphatase (EAP) knockout. TNAP-null mice are the canonical model of severe infantile hypophosphatasia: growth impairment, epileptic seizures and apnea, death before weaning, and abnormal bone mineralization with altered osteoblast morphology. MGI annotates this genotype to the MP *level* branch (MP:0002966, decreased circulating alkaline phosphatase level).

An independently derived TNAP knockout, curated separately from the Alpl<tm1Jlm> line above rather than merged with it, because the two differ on a substantive point: this line is reported to have normal skeletal development, while the tm1Jlm line shows abnormal bone mineralization. This is the study that establishes the pyridoxal 5'-phosphate mechanism behind the seizures - elevated serum PLP, reduced brain GABA, and rescue by pyridoxal administration - which the tm1Jlm report does not test.
